subject.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the new core conversations_* tool, Gateway protocol, plugin SDK, and v11 storage contract as the permanent transport-generic boundary between external conversations and local sessions?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and well-tested, but it creates durable public APIs and migration behavior across core, plugins, clients, and stored state; tests cannot determine whether this is the long-term product and ownership boundary maintainers want.

options.title: Approve the core contract
options.body: Accept the transport-generic conversation boundary after conflicts are resolved and live Reef plus upgrade proof confirms the intended compatibility behavior.

options.title: Narrow before adoption
options.body: Keep existing message/session surfaces and first land only the minimum generic seam or Reef-specific implementation needed to prove the abstraction before committing public APIs and schema.

recommendation.title: Approve the core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the transport-generic conversation boundary after conflicts are resolved and live Reef plus upgrade proof confirms the intended compatibility behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the linked design, authored the branch, and have recent mainline session/transcript architecture history.
